findings.title: Stale operator cell or prefer in SQLite makes the daemon fail at startup, with no CLI/API way to recover
findings.detail: The RuntimePolicy constructor re-validates every stored routing_cells row through `this.groups(...)` (validatePolicy against the current catalog) and every stored prefer through `validatePrefer`, and throws on the first failure. The Factory constructor builds RuntimePolicy without a try/catch, so the daemon fails to start. The only remedies are `limitless routing reset` and `DELETE /api/routing/...`, and both need the running daemon. The operator would have to edit SQLite by hand. The catalog changes routinely: models get retired into REMOVED_MODELS, config.toml models or providers get removed, and parts 3/4 make it runtime-driven. A cell that was valid when set can therefore brick the next

I reproduced this with a probe test that stores a cell for a model

findings.title: Any routing edit aborts every waiting slot acquisition in every run, including unrelated roles
findings.detail: `router.policyRevision` is a single global AbortController. It is aborted on every setPolicy, whatever cell changed, and on every setPreferProviders. Each run that is queued in tracker.acquire/acquireFirst is aborted and re-routed, and it loses its place in the provider queue. An edit to `triage.trivial` therefore reshuffles queued implement and review calls on the same providers, and they rejoin at the back of the queue.
findings.failure_scenario: Several runs are queued for a busy provider, and the operator edits an unrelated cell such as `chat.default`. Every queued call is aborted, re-routed and re-queued, so FIFO fairness is lost and the waits restart.

findings.title: Edited-cell marker is never cleared, so an implementer the edit did not remove still loses stickiness
findings.detail: `changedCells` only grows. Once a cell has been edited during the daemon's lifetime, or has an operator override at startup, any `c.prefer` not present in that cell's groups loses its preference and pin. Implementers often come from escalation beyond the policy list (minTier adds catalog models) or from a persisted explicit effort. Those were never in the cell, so the operator did not remove them. Before this change they stayed pinned; now an unrelated edit, or even a reset back to the original value, unpins them for the rest of the process.
findings.failure_scenario: A run escalated to model C via minTier; C is not in implement.medium. The operator adds model D to implement.medium. On the next implement round, preference C is cleared, so the run can switch implementers even though C was never removed.

findings.title: Validation errors are raw zod issue JSON dumps
findings.detail: `groups()` wraps `String(error)` from zod, so API and CLI users get a multi-line JSON array of issues (as seen in the probe output `implement.medium: [ {...`). The message does name the cell, and the inner message carries the reason, but this is hard to read in the CLI.

findings.title: A CI classification error on one PR aborts observation of all later PRs in the repo, permanently if the error is deterministic

Because ciPending is persisted as true and survives while the head is the same (`same && prev?.ciPending`), the same PR throws again on every poll. findings.title: Retry with different models pins every role when the run had no pinned models
findings.detail: When `run.models` is empty, the picker is prefilled with the current effective chain for every RUN_ROLE, and that whole map is sent to `/api/runs/:id/retry`. `app.retryRun` uses `models` as the new run's full model map. The `runtime_models` row therefore stays in the DB forever, and every daemon start prints the redundancy warning. Neither the warning nor EVIDENCE.md gives the operator a way to clear it. A literal model id inside Factory construction is also inconsistent with the rest of the catalog code, which is data-driven.

findings.failure_scenario: Persist triage.default = ["codex/legacy@high"] while that model is absent. Start successfully, then add codex/legacy with supportedEfforts = ["none"]. The add succeeds, but the next daemon startup fails.

gold.summary: Raw process output is cut before gate credential redaction can match a boundary-spanning secret.

findings.title: Redaction happens after the process runner has already truncated output
findings.detail: runProcess retains only the last 64,000 raw characters. The helper therefore cannot recognize a credential split at that earlier boundary. Stripping terminal sequences afterward can bring the surviving credential fragment into the final 6,000-character output, which consumers store and forward. A direct bun subprocess probe produced {"outputStart":"9-ABCDEFGHzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz","length":6000,"leakedSuffix":true,"redacted":false}. This violates the requested redact-before-truncate guarantee.
findings.failure_scenario: Register synthetic-boundary-secret-409-ABCDEFGH, then have a gate print that credential followed by 14,500 repetitions of ESC[0m and 5,990 z characters. The raw process tail cuts through the credential; normalization removes the escape sequences, and GateResult.output exposes 9-ABCDEFGH without a re

gold.summary: Lossy excerpt line framing prevents matching multiline credentials before storage.
Failure excerpt collection retains unbounded bytes on very long output lines.

findings.title: Privacy filter now withholds any text that contains the literal "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains "[redacted]". This applies to every MCP tool response field and to digest output, not only gate output. Text that was already safely redacted, such as agent errors redacted by the harnesses or run errors, and any text that simply mentions "[redacted]" (an issue body, a diff, a review finding) is now hidden completely instead of being shown in redacted form. The request never asked for this. Gate output reaching MCP is already redacted by this change, so redacted text was already safe to show. No test covers the new behaviour.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran `HOME=$TMPDIR/rv bun q.ts` on `privateOutputData({ error: "auth failed for token [redacted]; retry" }, loadOutputPrivacy())`. It printed `{ error: "[withheld: private text]", note: "ok" }`. Before the change, the redacted error message was returned.

findings.title: redactGateData is applied to whole API, prompt, report and state payloads and changes data that is not gate output
findings.detail: The request asks to redact once, where runGates builds a check's result, in about 30 source lines. Instead, redactGateData does a JSON round-trip with a replacer and is applied to every HTTP JSON response and SSE message, to every artifact body, to RunContext.state at construction, to cached stage values, and to implement, review and verify prompt inputs and report inputs. Side effects: (1) every string in those payloads, including user prompts, specs and logs, gets stripVTControlCharacters plus credential redaction; (2) any object with `ok` and `output` keys gains a `confinementError` field, which changes API shapes; (3) JSON artifacts served by /api/runs/:id/artifacts are re-serialized, so
findings.failure_scenario: An HTTP client fetching any JSON artifact gets minified JSON instead of the stored file. Any API object with `ok` and `output` keys gains `confinementError: false`. A user prompt containing ANSI escape sequences reaches the implementer prompt and the PR report with those sequences stripped.

findings.title: FailureExcerpts no longer caps line length and re-joins every retained line on each new line
findings.detail: The old 8,000-character cap per line was removed, so up to 39 or more lines of any length are kept in memory. Once the line limit is reached, every observed line triggers `redactGateOutput(this.lines.join("\n"))` over all retained lines, which costs O(40 × line length) per line. In my test with 5,000 lines of 20 KB each, extractFailures took 574 ms, against 116 ms at base. The cost grows with output size and with the number of registered credential variants.
findings.failure_scenario: A gate that prints thousands of very long lines (for example minified bundle output) makes the run noticeably slower and retains much more memory than before.

findings.title: `confinementError` is now always written, reversing a documented compatibility choice
findings.detail: The removed comment said the field is present only when set, so that results stay readable by strict schemas and older releases. The change now always writes `confinementError: false`, and `confinementFailed` treats an explicit `false` as authoritative, so it no longer checks the output text. No test covers older readers.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release or a strict schema that rejects unknown or always-present fields reads a gate result written by this version.

gold.summary: Redacting the carry early emits suffixes of overlapping registered credentials.
ANSI stripping after framing and tail cuts leaves accidental credential fragments visible.

findings.title: Defer replacement of credentials that overlap an incomplete longer credential
findings.detail: Redacting the pending buffer before resolving incomplete matches destroys longer credential prefixes. A shorter registered credential is replaced immediately, so subsequent chunks cannot match the longer credential and its suffix escapes into gate results and downstream consumers. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-redaction-review.test.ts". The overlapping-credentials test failed with Expected: "[redacted]"; Received: "[redacted]-private-credential-suffix".
findings.failure_scenario: Register "synthetic-shared-prefix" and "synthetic-shared-prefix-private-credential-suffix", then emit the longer credential in two chunks split immediately after the shorter credential.

findings.title: Normalize terminal formatting before the process runner truncates output
findings.detail: redactGateStreams receives streams already truncated by runProcess. The runner redacts without stripping terminal controls, so formatting inside a credential prevents its match. If the runner drops its prefix, subsequent normalization cannot redact the remaining fragment. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/gate-redaction-review.test.ts". The normalization test failed with Expected to not contain: "credential-421"; Received: "ecret-credential-421". This fragment is in GateResult.output and consequently reaches storage, logs and model feedback.
findings.failure_scenario: Register "synthetic-colored-secret-credential-421". Emit its first 12 characters, an ANSI color sequence, its remaining characters, and 15,995 ANSI reset sequences. The 64,000-character runner tail cuts through the unrecognized credential; normalization then exposes its suffix.

gold.summary: Configuration errors and encoded feed diagnostics can disclose registered secrets.
A failure after configuration replacement leaves initialization partially applied.
Doctor omits health probes for implicit providers and presets lacking an explicit health URL.
The command fake permits mutating operations during read-only diagnosis.
The registration test does not exercise preservation of existing vendor settings.

findings.title: Apply new configuration to an already healthy daemon
findings.detail: Init writes missing provider and merge settings but skips service installation whenever the original daemon check passed. The daemon loads configuration at startup and has no reload path, so init reports success while it continues using the old settings. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected to contain: "install"; Received: ["write /fake/config/config.toml", "write /fake/home/smoke-last.json"]`.
findings.failure_scenario: Run init against a healthy daemon with a partial config, adding a detected local provider or filling the missing merge policy. The written settings remain inactive until a separate restart.

findings.title: Do not silently omit provider health diagnosis
findings.detail: Provider health checks only exist when health_url is explicitly supplied. Valid configurations, including the OpenRouter preset, can omit it, leaving doctor to report key presence without testing whether the provider answers. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed `provider checks: [{"id":"provider:remote:key","status":"ok","message":"KEY present"}]` and failed the assertion that a provider health result exists.
findings.failure_scenario: Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider with an unreachable base_url and a present API key but no health_url. Doctor produces no health warning for that provider.

findings.title: Smoke-test the effective configured providers
findings.detail: The production smoke adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts, which selects providers, endpoints and models from the static catalog. Newly detected local providers are never exercised, and configured endpoint overrides are ignored. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/smoke-review.test.ts"` used fake harnesses and a zero execution budget to inspect scheduled checks; it listed only built-in provider rows and failed `Expected: true; Received: false` for inclusion of configured local-1234.
findings.failure_scenario: Init adds local-1234 from its model listing, but its inference endpoint is broken. Smoke checks never call that provider, so setup can report success without validating it.

findings.title: Check access to newly selected repositories before writing
findings.detail: Doctor runs before repository selection and only reads repositories already in the original config. Fresh --repo arguments receive syntax validation but no access or SSO check before configuration is written. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed `GitHub commands: [["gh","auth","status"]]` and failed the assertion that `gh api repos/restricted/private` was called.
findings.failure_scenario: On an empty config, run init --yes --repo restricted/private with an authenticated GitHub account lacking access or organization SSO authorization. Init writes the repository and proceeds without detecting the failure.

findings.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
findings.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with a hardcoded skipped message. Init never asks for or persists the requested choice. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed questions for repositories, merge policy and MCP only, then failed the discreet-question assertion with `Expected: true; Received: false`.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init expecting to select discreet mode, or an agent uses --yes expecting its default to be configured. Neither path configures it.

gold.summary: Nesting Seatbelt around internally sandboxed CLIs prevents tool-enabled invocations from starting.
Scanning ordinary agent output for sandbox diagnostics can discard successful invocations.
Ordinary gate output mentioning sandbox failures can turn a successful check into a confinement error.
The live confinement smoke accepts refusal even when enforcement should work.

findings.title: Detect executable substitutions inside quoted shell arguments
findings.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque tokens, so executable command substitutions are ignored. Unquoted heredoc bodies are also discarded as literal data despite permitting command substitution. Reproduction: bun -e 'import {signalCommand} from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(pkill -f marker)\""), true)' fails with `AssertionError: false !== true`. This only analyzes the string; it does not execute pkill. Such tool calls produce no signal warning, event-log warning, or run.warning feed item.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent submits Bash command `echo "$(pkill -f marker)"` or an unquoted heredoc containing `$(kill 123)`. The shell attempts the signal, but signalCommand returns false and the attempt is absent from warning reporting.

gold.summary: A bare executable magic match rejects valid image bytes with an incidental signature.

findings.title: Restore all requested inert-media extensions
findings.detail: INERT_MEDIA_PATH includes only five image extensions, excluding explicitly required formats such as PDF, WOFF2 and MP4. The new tests even assert that fonts, audio and PDFs must block, contradicting the request. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output included: FAIL pdf addition exemptions actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"asset.pdf"}] expected=[]; FAIL woff2 addition exemptions actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"asset.woff2"}] expected=[]. Edits failed identically.
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a valid PDF or WOFF2 file without Allow: binary; the audit incorrectly blocks it.

findings.title: Do not classify ordinary text by embedded signature substrings
findings.detail: isForbiddenFormat searches entire blobs for short signatures and ordinary strings, and repos.ts removes matching files from the text classification. Consequently, fully reviewable source and documentation require a binary allowance. This also explains the automated binary flags on this patch's text source files. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output: FAIL reviewable source is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"README.md"},{"rule":"binary-content","file":"country.ts"},{"rule":"binary-content","file":"format.ts"}] expected=[].
findings.failure_scenario: Commit README.md containing 'A recipe for custard.', country.ts containing export const country = "MZ";, or source containing the literal "%PDF-".

findings.title: Keep executable text scripts outside the binary allowance
findings.detail: modeRequiresAllowance unconditionally marks every changed 100755 file as binary, including existing shell scripts whose text is completely visible. It also marks removal of an executable bit when the blob is unchanged. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output: FAIL reviewable executable shell script is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[]; FAIL edit existing executable shell script is text actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[]; FAIL remove executable bit on shell script actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"hello.sh"}] expected=[].
findings.failure_scenario: Add or edit a normal executable shell script, or chmod an unchanged script from 755 to 644, without Allow: binary.

findings.title: Do not reject valid PNGs with ordinary metadata
findings.detail: The new PNG parser rejects valid chunks outside its small whitelist, including standard tEXt comment metadata. Thus even the retained PNG extension does not satisfy the requested exemption. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/audit-review.ts". Output: PNG base valid=true; PNG with valid tEXt valid=false; FAIL PNG with ordinary Comment metadata is inert actual=[{"rule":"binary-content","file":"asset.png"}] expected=[]. The reproduction adds a correctly framed and checksummed Comment chunk to the supplied valid PNG fixture.
findings.failure_scenario: Add a valid PNG containing a standard tEXt chunk with 'Comment\0ordinary image'; the audit incorrectly blocks it.

gold.summary: Detached descendants survive invocation cleanup and keep modifying the worktree.
Process cleanup returns while owned descendants are still alive.
Discarding changes replaces the cleanup error that should trigger round recovery.

findings.title: Final cleanup can mask the recoverable cleanup error
findings.detail: After checkoutCommitted exhausts its clean retry and throws WorktreeCleanError, the gates' finally block calls discardChanges. If untracked files remain and that cleanup also fails, its CommandError replaces WorktreeCleanError. This handler rethrows it, failing the run instead of advancing the round. Reproduced with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-clean.ts"`: `checkout alone: WorktreeCleanError round handler catches: true` followed by `with gates finally: CommandError round handler catches: false`.
findings.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's untracked output cannot be removed. Both clean -ffdxq attempts fail, then discardChanges encounters the same output and clean -fdq fails.

findings.title: Process-group termination still leaves detached descendants alive
findings.detail: killTree only signals the original process group. Descendants that create another session or process group survive, and the new wait returns immediately when the original group disappears. This leaves the requested whole-tree teardown incomplete. Reproduced with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-process.ts"`, spawning a Python child with start_new_session=True: output was `{"exitCode":0,"childStillAlive":true}`, followed by `error: Background descendant survived invocation completion`. This limitation predates the diff but remains an unmet requirement of this fix.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent tool launches a detached background writer with redirected stdio. The agent exits normally or is stopped; runProcess resolves while the writer continues modifying the worktree during cleanup.

gold.summary: Run-wide scratch roots let one invocation cleanup kill another invocation writer.
A recycled leader PID claims unrelated processes through reused group or session identifiers.

findings.title: Directory membership can cause teardown to kill unrelated processes
findings.detail: An unmarked orphan born after invocation startup is treated as owned solely because its cwd matches an invocation directory. This does not establish ancestry. An isolated fixture launched an independent shell from the reviewer process while runProcess was running; teardown killed that shell. Exact check: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501/review-process-membership.ts unrelated`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated","exitCode":0,"alive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: independent unmarked process was killed`.
findings.failure_scenario: An independent background shell becomes orphaned in the same directory after a command starts. When that command ends, teardown signals the independent shell.

findings.title: Detached shells outside the captured directories still outlive invocation shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery happens during shutdown, after detached descendants can lose their parent chain. A macOS shell with a hidden environment and cwd outside the captured roots is then omitted, and shutdown returns success. This leaves the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Exact check: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501/review-process-membership.ts descendant`. Output: `{"mode":"descendant","exitCode":0,"alive":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached background child outlived invocation`. A separate check reproduced this with the invocation environment inherited.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer launches a detached background shell in a temporary directory and exits after it starts. The shell can continue writing to absolute worktree paths after runProcess returns and cleanup begins.

gold.summary: Pre-aborted shutdown with failed leader inspection references timer cleanup before initialization and never settles.

findings.title: Working directory does not prove ownership of an orphan
findings.detail: The orphan fallback claims any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd matches an invocation directory, even without ancestry or an invocation marker. This kills unrelated processes. A temporary fixture launched an unrelated orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess was active. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" unrelated. Output: {"case":"unrelated","alive":false,"bytesWrittenAfterReturn":0}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup' (exit 1).
findings.failure_scenario: Another invocation or user launches a detached, environment-cleared process in the same worktree after this invocation starts. Its parent exits. Finishing this invocation kills that unrelated orphan.

findings.title: Detached descendants can survive confirmed shutdown
findings.detail: Discovery misses descendants that clear their environment, create a separate session, and leave the invocation directories before their parent exits. runProcess then returns successfully while they continue writing into the worktree through absolute paths. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" descendant. Output: {"case":"descendant","alive":true,"bytesWrittenAfterReturn":2}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: invocation descendant must stop before runProcess returns' (exit 1). This preserves the cleanup race the request requires fixing.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached background writer with env {}, cwd /private/tmp, and an absolute output path inside the worktree, then exits. Cleanup starts while the writer remains alive.

gold.summary: A single extracted test command is treated as proof of a multi-step criterion.

findings.title: Require coverage of the complete verification instructions
findings.detail: The regex extracts one Bun command and ignores additional prose instructions, then applyGateEvidence marks the entire criterion met. A passing loopback test therefore also satisfies a separate outbound-denial check that never ran. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-AAmrsP/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts multi`. Output: `expected blocked; actual met`, followed by `error: Unverified criterion was marked met`.
findings.failure_scenario: Instructions are `Run bun test loopback.test.ts, then manually verify outbound connections stay denied.` Gates pass loopback.test.ts, while the verifier reports the additional check blocked. The factory marks the whole criterion met without outbound-denial evidence.

findings.title: Require positive test execution evidence for targeted commands
findings.detail: The exact-file branch accepts a successful process whenever its output lacks failure or skip markers, even with no passing tests. Confirmed that Bun exits 0 and emits only its version and file header when a test module calls process.exit(0). Those actual output bytes are accepted as coverage. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-AAmrsP/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts zero`. Output: `expected blocked; actual met`, followed by `error: Unverified criterion was marked met`.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted loopback test exits successfully during initialization before registering or executing tests. Its gate passes with empty passedFiles, and a blocked verifier criterion is nevertheless converted to met.

gold.summary: Free-text claim detection still lets model wording steer gate-evidence substitution.

findings.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable all gate evidence
findings.detail: passed() rejects any check containing skipped files, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to pass this predicate. Consequently, a passing loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined always sets, so ordinary confined suite results retain the original verification blockage. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `unrelated skip: blocked` despite recorded passing coverage for test/loopback.test.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: Confined bun test passes test/loopback.test.ts and skips test/sandbox.test.ts. The verifier cannot bind loopback and reports the loopback criterion blocked. The engine refuses substitution and ends verification as needs_human.

findings.title: A general note mentioning gates invalidates independent evidence
findings.detail: Every criterion is scanned against the entire verify.notes field. Any standalone mention of gates therefore converts every met criterion to blocked, even when the note explicitly disclaims reliance on gates and each criterion contains independently observed evidence. Isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `independent observation with notes: blocked` for notes saying 'I did not rely on gates; independently inspected the implementation.'
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier independently validates all criteria, then mentions gates in its general notes. Criteria requiring inspection or commands unsupported by gate substitution become blocked and can terminate an otherwise successful run as needs_human.

findings.title: Exact command matching bypasses recorded file coverage
findings.detail: When requested and selected arguments match, covers() returns success without checking passedFiles. Bun treats bare test arguments as filename filters, so matching command strings do not prove the requested file ran. In a TMPDIR fixture containing only unrelated/test/loopback.test.ts, `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` exited successfully and printed `(pass) unrelated`. Feeding that result and its accurate coverage into the helper with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-gate-evidence.js"` returned `wrong file ran: met` for the missing test/loopback.test.ts criterion.
findings.failure_scenario: The criterion requires test/loopback.test.ts, but only unrelated/test/loopback.test.ts exists. The gate command matches and passes the unrelated file; the verifier reports an environment block. The engine incorrectly marks the required criterion met and attaches authoritative gate provenance.

gold.summary: An inherited Git configuration selector redirects trusted SSH lookup into the checkout.
Trusted remote-dependent credential and SSH settings no longer apply during push.
Manual landing publishes a fork branch to the upstream repository.
Forcing HTTPS during manual push bypasses working SSH authentication.

findings.title: Preserve trusted remote-conditional credential configuration
findings.detail: Replacing the common directory removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global `includeIf "hasconfig:remote.*.url:…"` blocks. Credential helpers and SSH settings in those blocks consequently disappear. An offline credential-fill probe succeeded before isolation with `username=test` and `password=trusted`, but running it through `bash scripts/push-git.sh <probe> push https://example.invalid/repo.git HEAD:refs/heads/main` returned 128: `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://example.invalid': terminal prompts disabled`. This violates the requirement to preserve existing global credential setup.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner's global config conditionally includes their credential helper based on remote.origin.url. Ordinary Git authenticates successfully, but factory delivery and land pushes lose the helper and fail authentication.

findings.title: Preserve reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
findings.detail: The isolated repository copies only objects, refs and packed-refs, then declares repository format 0. It omits reftable storage and `extensions.refStorage`, so source references cannot resolve in a reftable repository. In a fixture created with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push --no-follow-tags "$url" HEAD:refs/heads/using-head` returned 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`; the same Git push without the wrapper succeeded. Normal delivery still calls pushBranch with `HEAD` in src/pipeline/engine.ts.
findings.failure_scenario: A factory repository uses reftable storage, for example through trusted global init.defaultRefFormat configuration. Normal delivery pushes HEAD through the wrapper and fails despite a valid commit and reachable local remote.

gold.summary: Manual push reloads mutable clone configuration after its final validation snapshot.
Inherited Git configuration causes validation and push to inspect different settings.
An exact upstream URL requirement rejects supported forks and alternate origin spellings.

findings.title: Delivery and land-queue pushes still execute repository-configured commands
findings.detail: The change only modifies the manual landing script. pushBranch and pushExistingBranch, which also serves the land queue, still read repository command and URL-rewrite settings without isolating trusted scopes or disabling ext transport. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-push-probe.ts"` against local bare remotes printed `pushBranch: repository command executed = true ; exact SHA = true` and `pushExistingBranch: repository command executed = true ; exact SHA = true`. The probe planted a repository URL rewrite to an ext transport script and enabled that protocol locally. Both APIs executed the script.
findings.failure_scenario: PR code plants repository-level URL rewriting and protocol settings. Delivery or the land queue subsequently invokes a push using that repository, executing the planted transport command.

findings.title: The push still trusts repository config after its final snapshot
findings.detail: Validation and snapshot comparison do not isolate the subsequent push: it still targets `origin` and rereads mutable repository config. A process left running by the unconfined checks can install receivepack or pushurl after the snapshot. The local probe `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` used the script's actual functions and emulated that write between comparison and push. It printed `post-snapshot-write: exit 0` and `repository receivepack executed = True ; exact SHA = True`. Thus the pinned SHA does not prevent command execution in the protected window.
findings.failure_scenario: A background process started during bun run check writes remote.origin.receivepack after config_after is captured but before git push reads the config.

findings.title: The allowlist blocks landing repositories with harmless local settings
findings.detail: The validator rejects every local key outside a narrow clone-metadata list, including ordinary user.name, user.email, and additional remotes. This changes normal landing behavior instead of excluding untrusted config only for the push. Running `python3 "$TMPDIR/review-config-probe.py"` with local user.name printed `local-identity: exit 1`, `Repository git config key user.name is not allowed; refusing to land`, and `Cannot validate repository git config; refusing to land`. The script stops before checks or publication even though this setting cannot execute a push command.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer configures a repository-specific commit identity with git config user.name, then invokes land-pr.sh; landing immediately fails.

gold.summary: Unresolved tool calls accumulate without a bound during a live invocation.

findings.title: Missing results no longer count while the invocation runs
findings.detail: Calls awaiting results are excluded from counting, and an unresolved call also blocks later completions of its key. Six identical unresolved calls therefore never stop the active invocation. Subsequent calls can evict them before finish(), permanently losing the loop. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); let reason = null; for (let i=0; i<6; i++) reason=d.observe("shell", {command:"poll"}, String(i)); for (let i=0; i<12; i++) d.observe("Read", {path:i}, `read-${i}`); assert.equal(d.finish(), "repeated the same shell call 6 times");' Output: AssertionError, actual n
findings.failure_scenario: An agent emits six identical shell calls with distinct IDs and no results, then twelve unrelated calls. Neither the sixth repeated call nor invocation completion reports the loop.

gold.summary: A completed parallel call is classified as repetitive before unresolved predecessors establish progress.

findings.title: Do not finalize pending results when another tool starts
findings.detail: Every observe() calls reconcile(true), treating a pending threshold result as finished merely because another tool starts. Both harnesses then abort immediately, so a changed result cannot establish progress. The new 'pending threshold result' test explicitly expects this incorrect cutoff. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import {LoopDetector} from "./src/harness/types.ts"; import {strictEqual} from "node:assert"; const d=new LoopDetector(100); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){d.observe("shell","poll",`${i}`);d.observeResult(`${i}`,"waiting");} d.observe("shell","poll","sixth"); strictEqual(d.observe("Read","file","other"),null); d.observeResult("sixth","progress");' Output: AssertionError: Expected values
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return 'waiting'. A sixth poll starts and will return 'progress', but an unrelated Read starts before that result arrives. The detector reports a loop and both harnesses cancel the progressing invocation.

gold.summary: A historical policy edit keeps invalidating implementer selections made after that edit.

findings.title: Existing config-cache test fails on both base and HEAD
findings.detail: Command: bun test test/git-integrity.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'an unchanged worktree lists its config once'. Output: Expected length: 1; Received length: 2. The identical assertion fails on base commit 0de5e94, so this is not a routing regression.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the isolated unchanged-worktree test in this environment observes two config listings instead of one.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Keep previously tried implementers excluded after escalation
findings.detail: The exclusion of triedImplementers applies only to the invocation that escalates. Subsequent rounds pass only a preference for the current implementer, allowing capacity fallback to resurrect an earlier, exhausted candidate. A temporary fake-harness regression run with `bun test "$TMPDIR/chain-regression.test.ts" -t 'review regression'` failed with `IMPLEMENT_CALLS ["alpha/m","alpha/m","beta/m","beta/m","alpha/m"]` and `Expected to not contain: "alpha/m"; Received: [ "beta/m", "beta/m", "alpha/m" ]`.
findings.failure_scenario: Pin implement to [A, B]. A fails gates for two rounds, causing escalation to B. B fails gates once, then returns quota on its next invocation. The run invokes A again instead of entering needs_human because its chain is exhausted.

gold.summary: A fixed review-time cutoff excludes worktrees created before the sidecar-writing release actually started.

findings.title: Do not equate the sidecar commit timestamp with installation time

findings.detail: The isolated directory preserves objects and file-based refs but omits reftable storage and extensions.refStorage. findings.detail: Replacing the common config removes remote URLs used to evaluate trusted global includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url conditions. findings.detail: The previous push used origin's configured transport. findings.detail: The temporary common directory preserves only files-based refs and object-format metadata. It omits extensions.refStorage and reftable storage. Output: 'six unresolved calls: null', followed by the assertion error. A second direct check c
findings.failure_scenario: An agent emits six identical calls with distinct IDs and no results. Both harnesses continue instead of stopping at six. If twelve unrelated calls follow, the repeated calls are evicted and the invocation can finish without any loop detection.

gold.summary: Against an older daemon that ignores the new repo parameter, limitless_list_runs returns other repositories' runs as matches, because the proxy never checks that the filter was applied.

findings.detail: The proxy relies entirely on the daemon honoring the new repo query parameter. The base-version daemon ignores it, so a newer CLI connected to the running previous release returns unrelated repositories and computes hasMore from those results. A read-only `bun run -` probe executing the new httpBackend against the extracted base GET handler returned [{"id":"new-other","repoSlug":"other/repo"},{"id":"older-requested","repoSlug":"wanted/repo"}] for repo=wanted/repo.

findings.title: Compact output still includes an unbounded dependency array
findings.detail: compactRun copies every dependsOn entry. Dependency counts have no input limit, so clipping title and error does not bound default output size. A read-only `bun run -` probe executing the extracted compactRun with 1,200 dependencies and short scalar fields printed `compact get_run size with 1200 dependencies: 30186`, exceeding both newly tested byte budgets before MCP envelope overhead.

findings.title: Repository filtering silently fails against the previous daemon
findings.detail: The proxy relies entirely on the new HTTP repo parameter. The base daemon ignores that parameter and limits across all repositories, so a newer MCP client returns unrelated runs and incorrect hasMore information. A focused check using the actual httpBackend with a base-compatible response failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review.ts" skew` printed `requested target/repo; received: [{"id":"other","repoSlug":"other/repo"}]`, followed by `AssertionError: false == true`.
findings.failure_scenario: A newer stdio MCP client connects to the previous running daemon and calls limitless_list_runs with repo set to target/repo while newer runs belong to other/repo.

findings.title: Compact output retains an unbounded dependency array
findings.detail: Both default inspection tools copy every dependency ID into their compact output. Dependency validation imposes no count limit, so valid fan-in runs still exceed the intended byte budgets. A focused check executing the actual compactRun function failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review.ts" size` printed `compactRun bytes: 33185; expected < 4096`, followed by `AssertionError: false == true`. Five such runs also exceed the list test's 16 KB budget.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid run depends on 1,000 existing runs. Default get_run returns over 33 KB before adding state and land information; a default list containing several such runs is substantially larger.

gold.summary: A pinned candidate slot deadline exits without recording the chain-exhaustion question.

findings.title: Pinned verify chain clears excludeModels, so the environment-blocked retry reruns the same verifier
findings.detail: For the verify role, `excludeModels` is not the implementer's checkpoint. It is the first verifier's model, passed by `verifyAttempt(1, [firstModel])` (engine.ts:1553) so the environment-blocked retry gets a different verifier. The change sets `excludeModels: undefined` whenever verify has a chain, so the retry picks the first chain entry again even when the chain lists a fallback. The warning check at context.ts:634 then treats that excluded model as an avoided implementer checkpoint and logs "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint (...) because this run pinned it", which is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: Run with `models.verify = ["A", "B"]`. The first verify attempt returns only blocked criteria, so the engine retries with excludeModels=[A]. The chain path clears that, A is invoked again instead of B, and a misleading 'implementer's vendor/checkpoint' warning is logged.

findings.title: A pinned chain throws away a decision model's last-resort result
findings.detail: `if (!target && lastResort && !chain)` stops pinned runs from using a last-resort result. That result comes from a model inside the chain (a triage decision model that declined with `lastResort: true`), so using it would not be a fallback outside the chain. As written, a pinned triage experiment on a decision model that declines with low ambiguity goes to needs_human, while the same model in policy would have finished triage.
findings.failure_scenario: `--model triage=<decision-model>`. The model declines with `decline.lastResort=true`, no other chain entry exists, and the run goes to needs_human instead of using the pinned model's own triage.

findings.title: In configured panel review mode, a one-entry review chain can deadlock on the verifier's hard exclusion
findings.detail: Under a review chain the panel verifier still routes with `excludeModels` set to the models that raised candidates (`verifierConstraints`), and the chain path does not relax it for the review role. If the chain has one entry, the finder that raised candidates is the only candidate and is excluded, so the verifier has no target and the run goes to needs_human. Production defaults to single mode, so this only affects configured panel systems.
findings.failure_scenario: reviewSystem mode=panel, `models.review=["alpha/m"]`. The alpha finder raises a candidate, the verifier excludes alpha, and the run goes to needs_human.

findings.title: Pinned-chain warning always blames the implementer's vendor
findings.detail: The message says "the implementer's vendor/checkpoint" for every role except holdout. In the panel verifier, `avoidVendor` is the set of vendors that raised candidates, not the implementer's vendor, so the warning names the wrong reason.
findings.failure_scenario: In a panel review whose verifier chain lands on a vendor that raised a candidate, the logged reason says 'implementer's vendor'.

gold.summary: Arbitrary assertion text mentioning a timeout is classified as a transient CI failure.
Retry eligibility ignores security failures outside the selected error line.
A paused PR is not inspected again when main recovers without another PR change.
An accepted rerun with a lost response is never reconciled to its later result.

findings.detail:
`classifyCi` reports problems by throwing: `Incomplete CI inspection`, `Ambiguous originating CI job`, `Incomplete failing check`, zod parse errors, and others. `record` does not catch them, so the error escapes `observe` and the per-repo catch in `tick` swallows it. `observe` calls `record` serially for each PR in the batch, so every PR after the failing one goes unrecorded that cycle. Nothing records its merge or close, its CI or review changes, or its access state.

Because `save()` writes `ciPending: true` before the classifier runs, the next poll retries the same inspection. When the cause is persistent, the repository's later PRs are starved indefinitely. Persistent causes include:
- j
findings.failure_scenario: Repository has PRs A and B, in that order in the batch. A's failing job logs return 410, or A's workflow has two jobs with the same name and one times out. B is merged. Every poll throws while inspecting A, so B's `pr.merged` and its run-merge reconciliation never happen.

findings.title: Wrong failure lines in the ledger, and passing output can make a failure 'transient'
findings.detail:
`ciSignature` takes the first log line that matches `timed out after|##[error]|\b(error|fail|failed|failure)\b`. In real test output, passing test names and setup lines often contain those words, so the recorded 'failing test or error line' is frequently a passing test. Separately, `transient` is `/timed out after/i.test(log)` over the entire log. Any passing test or log line mentioning 'timed out after' turns a deterministic failure into a transient one. That spends the one-rerun cap and delays `ci.needs_fix` by a full CI cycle. Since the signature is also the ledger and dedup key, flake evidence gets attributed to the wrong test.

findings.failure_scenario: A bun or jest job with a genuine assertion failure, whose passing tests include one named '...timed out after...'. The job is rerun as transient and fails again. The ledger and feed record the passing test's name as the failure signature.

findings.title: Feed excerpt is the start of the job log, not the failure
findings.detail: `emit` is called with `log || f.line` and stores `quote(excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000))`. That is the first 2000 characters of the whole Actions job log. Actions logs begin with runner, OS and image preamble, plus checkout and setup groups, so the excerpt in `ci.needs_fix` almost never contains the failure. That makes it useless to whoever investigates the item.
findings.failure_scenario: Any `ci.needs_fix` from an Actions job whose log is longer than about 2000 characters: the excerpt shows 'Current runner version ... Runner Image ...' rather than the failing assertion.

findings.title: New `[github] ci_reruns` switch is not documented
findings.detail: The GUIDE config table documents every `[github]` key (`poll`, `poll_seconds`), but the new `ci_reruns` switch is missing. It defaults to on and triggers paid CI reruns, so operators need to know it exists.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator who wants to stop automatic reruns has no documented way to find the switch.

findings.title: A table introduced by this change is split across two migrations; change is about twice the budget
findings.detail: `ci_failures` is created in `20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql`, and this same change then adds `rerun_job` in a second migration. Neither has shipped, so the column belongs in the CREATE TABLE. The change is also about 500 source lines against a requested budget of about 250. The classifier is dense, with many inline guard-and-throw paths, which makes it hard to review and maintain.
findings.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; this adds schema churn and maintenance cost.

gold.summary: Catalog mutation can invalidate a shadowed retained policy and prevent the daemon from restarting.

findings.title: Persisted runtime models crash Factory boot on a collision or a missing provider
findings.detail:
At startup the Factory merges `store.runtimeModels()` and throws `catalog collision: ` if the id now matches a code or config model. It throws `unknown provider

` if the model's provider is no longer defined. Two normal workflows lead here. One is promoting a trialed runtime model into config.toml under the same id. The other is a later release adding the same model to the built-in catalog, which is the point of trying it at runtime first. Removing a config-defined provider that had runtime models also does it. In all three cases the daemon won't start. The API is the only way to remove runtime models and it is down too, so recovery needs hand-written SQL. The add-time collision check
findings.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a probe test in a TMPDIR copy. I ran `factory.catalog.add({...customModel, provider:'mac-mlx', id:'next'})`, then added `{id:'next'}` to mac-mlx's `[[providers.models]]` in config.toml and constructed a new Factory on the same database. It threw `Error: catalog collision: mac-

findings.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
findings.detail: `patch` merges `{...old, ...patch}` and runs the result through `mapFields`. That step drops `undefined` but keeps `null`, and `modelSchema.effort` is `.optional()`, so `{effort: null}` is rejected. JSON has no way to send `undefined`, so a default effort, once set, can only be removed by deleting and re-adding the model. Deletion is itself blocked while any policy cell names the model. GUIDE.md advises omitting the default effort for Claude-backed local servers, so an operator who set one by mistake is stuck.
findings.failure_scenario: Add `omlx/x` with `effort: "high"`, then send `PATCH /api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fx {"effort":null}`. It returns 400 `model.effort: invalid or missing field`, and the default effort can't be removed while a cell references the model.

findings.title: DELETE checks operator cells but not the evals policy overlay
findings.detail: `remove` checks only `store.routingCells()`. The evals overlay from `readPolicy(opts.policyPath, this.models, …)` is validated against a model list that includes runtime models, so it can name one. After such a model is deleted, routing skips the missing id for now. On the next restart, `readPolicy` validates the overlay against a catalog that no longer has the model and fails.
findings.failure_scenario: An evals policy file contains `triage.small: ["omlx/exp"]`, where omlx/exp is a runtime model, and the operator deletes omlx/exp. Deletion succeeds, and the next daemon start fails while validating the evals policy.

findings.title: Tests don't cover decoding of the encoded model id in the route
findings.detail: Model ids contain '/', so the CLI sends `/api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fnew`, and the handler uses `req.params.id` without decoding it. The test client applies `decodeURIComponent` before calling the handler, so the tests never check that Bun's router decodes `%2F` in params. If Bun doesn't, every CLI `remove` and API PATCH/DELETE fails with `missing catalog model omlx%2Fnew`. I couldn't check this because the sandbox blocks socket binding.
findings.failure_scenario: `limitless catalog remove omlx/new` sends `DELETE /api/catalog/models/omlx%2Fnew`. If Bun leaves the param undecoded, the server answers 400 `missing catalog model omlx%2Fnew`.

findings.title: Every health probe now publishes provider status, even when nothing changed
findings.detail: `probeProvider` now calls `this.publish(id)` on every probe, success or failure. Each publish also queries `served_models` through `status()`. Before this change, status was only pushed when health changed. Changes that matter are already covered by `recordDiscovery` and `setHealthy`.
findings.failure_scenario: With three probed local providers, SSE clients get three identical provider events per probe interval.

findings.title: Smoke now opens the production database and skips disabled providers
findings.detail: `main` builds `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations against the live database from the smoke script. It also now drops disabled providers and turns missing-provider errors into silent skips. Neither change is needed for the requested catalog-not-served check.
findings.failure_scenario: Running the deploy smoke check against new code applies this migration to the live database before the daemon restarts, and a provider that has been disabled is no longer smoke-tested.

gold.summary: Digest actions are derived from stale records instead of current unanswered and review state.
A historical failed review hides a later approval in MCP status.

findings.title: A blocked land stays in the digest after the PR is merged, closed or the run is resolved
findings.detail: The 'Blocked lands' group is cleared only by `land.queued` and `land.landed`. A blocked land entry is final in the queue. If someone then merges or closes the PR on GitHub, or resolves the run, the feed gets `pr.merged`/`pr.closed`/`run.merged`/`run.resolved` items with the same PR URL (`data.url`/`data.prUrl`), but none of them clear this group. The digest keeps reporting a blocked land until the consumer acknowledges past it. The PR-review group already handles `pr.merged`/`pr.closed`/`run.merged`, so the two groups are inconsistent.
findings.failure_scenario: Feed after the cursor contains [land.blocked {url: PR1}, pr.merged {url: PR1}, run.merged {prUrl: PR1}]. The probe output was 'Blocked lands: 1' with the item still listed.

findings.title: A PR resolved or cancelled outside the factory still shows as awaiting review
findings.detail: 'PRs awaiting review' is cleared by approval, merge, close and land events, but not by `run.resolved` (for example kind `wont_do`/`superseded`) or `run.cancelled`. Both carry `data.prUrl`, so they would hit the same key. After an operator resolves a run as won't-do, its PR stays in the review list.
findings.failure_scenario: Feed contains [run.pr_opened {prUrl: PR1}, run.resolved {prUrl: PR1, kind: 'wont_do'}]. The probe output was 'PRs awaiting review: 1'.

findings.title: Answered questions stay under 'Needs you' until the run finishes
findings.detail: `run.question` is cleared only by terminal run events. No feed item is emitted when a question is answered, so a run that was answered and is running again is still listed as needing the user until it succeeds, fails or is cancelled.
findings.failure_scenario: A run asks a question, the agent answers it and the run resumes. A new session's digest still says 'Needs you: 1' for that run.

findings.title: The Codex skill tells Codex to use consumer name 'claude'
findings.detail: The Codex copy of the skill is identical to the Claude one and recommends `limitless digest --consumer claude`. A Codex agent following it would share the Claude cursor name. That is harmless for the read-only digest, but it steers Codex toward a cursor whose acknowledgements belong to another agent.
findings.failure_scenario: A Codex session runs the digest and then uses consumer 'claude' with limitless_feed_ack, moving the Claude session's cursor forward.

gold.summary: Layered URL and Unicode encodings bypass the single-pass private-text decoder.

findings.title: If the privacy policy can't be read, tools that change state still act but hide their result
findings.detail: The CallTool handler now runs every tool and then, if `loadOutputPrivacy()` returned null, replaces the output of every tool except `limitless_status` with "Tool output withheld". So `limitless_create_run`, `limitless_land`, `limitless_review`, `limitless_answer_question` and `limitless_cancel_run` still make their change, but the agent gets no run id, land entry or approval back. The tool descriptions tell agents not to retry without inspecting state, but without the id they can't inspect it. This MCP-wide privacy layer, and the matching `\uXXXX` decoding added to the publication gate in src/gates/private.ts, were not asked for.
findings.failure_scenario: ~/.config/limitless/private-strings.txt is unreadable (for example a directory or invalid UTF-8). An agent calls `limitless_create_run`: the run is created, but the reply is {"message":"Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable."}. The agent has no id and may submit a duplicate.

findings.title: Digest lists a PR as awaiting review while its changes round is still running
findings.detail: For the 'PRs awaiting review' group, the digest only checks the approval and the land entry. It ignores `review.rounds`, so a PR whose "changes" verdict has started a review round that is still queued or running counts as awaiting review. For the same run, `limitless_status` (mcp-status.ts) says "Review changes in progress". I confirmed this with a probe: a feed holding run.pr_opened, plus detail with a stale approval and a round in status running, prints "PRs awaiting review: 1".
findings.failure_scenario: The agent sends `limitless_review` with verdict=changes and round 1 starts running. The next SessionStart digest still lists the PR under 'PRs awaiting review', so the agent may review an unchanged head again.

findings.title: limitless_status drops its state and next action when the privacy policy can't be read
findings.detail: With no privacy policy, `result()` returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. The `state` and `nextAction` strings are fixed text written in this file and contain no untrusted data, yet they are dropped. The request says status returns a plain-language state and the next action.
findings.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt is invalid UTF-8. `limitless_status` returns `{land:null, openQuestions:0}`, which doesn't tell the agent what state the run is in or what to do next.

findings.title: Codex skill tells Codex to use the Claude consumer name
findings.detail: The Codex skill is a copy of the Claude skill and says `limitless digest --consumer claude`. Following it, a Codex session would read the cursor of the Claude consumer, and might acknowledge on it, instead of using its own consumer.
findings.failure_scenario: A Codex agent follows the skill, runs the digest, then acks under 'claude', which moves the Claude session's feed cursor forward.

findings.title: Review and land return the backend result without schema validation
findings.detail: Every other tool checks the backend response against a zod schema before returning it, so a malformed response becomes a 'Malformed backend response' error. `limitless_review` and `limitless_land` return the raw `unknown` instead. Separately, the new server `instructions` text has no test.
findings.failure_scenario: An older daemon or a proxy returns an unexpected body from /api/land. The MCP tool passes it through as if it succeeded, instead of reporting a malformed response.

gold.summary: Queued chat dispatch uses a target whose origin became excluded after selection.
Queued eval dispatch does not revalidate origin eligibility after catalog changes.

findings.title: Smoke script refactor adds churn beyond the stated budget and changes how `--models` behaves
findings.detail: About 185 lines of scripts/smoke.ts were restructured into `explicitModelChecks` and `nativeChecks`, with target selection made lazy. Filtering excluded models before smoke makes live calls is consistent with "never call CN models". But `main()` now always runs `loadConfig()` before handling `--models`, and the explicit `--models` path now resolves against the config catalog and providers instead of the code-level MODELS/PROVIDERS. Those behaviour changes weren't requested, and together with the src changes they push the diff well past the roughly 200-source-line budget.
findings.failure_scenario: `bun scripts/smoke.ts --models codex/x@high` now requires a loadable config and resolves models from the config catalog. Before this change it used the built-in catalog regardless of config.

gold.summary: Forced-color Bun result markers are not recognized by failure extraction.

findings.title: bun's end-of-run recap of failed tests is counted again, using up the 10-failure cap and adding a false "left out" note
findings.detail: The failure regex matches every `(fail)` line, including the recap list (`N tests failed:` followed by one `(fail) name` per failure) that, according to the issue, bun prints at the end of long runs in this repository. Each recap line becomes another excerpt: the first one is "N tests failed:\n(fail) x" and the rest are the bare `(fail)` line. They count toward the 10-failure cap and the 8,000-character budget. With 6–9 real failures the recap fills the remaining slots, sets `omitted`, and the output ends with "[failure excerpts: diagnostic lines or failures left out]" although no real failure diagnostics were dropped. The request requires saying when something was left out, so this note is
findings.failure_scenario: Simulated input: 8 per-file blocks `error: eN\n(fail) tN`, then `3 tests failed:` and 8 recap `(fail) tN` lines. extractFailures returns the 8 real excerpts, then "3 tests failed:\n(fail) t1", "(fail) t2" and the "left out" note (verified with a probe script in TMPDIR).

findings.title: Strict eval GateResultSchema rejects gate results that carry the new `failures` field
findings.detail: GateResultSchema is a `z.strictObject` that lists `timedOut` and `confinementError` as optional fields precisely so stored results stay readable. The diff adds `failures` to GateResult but not to this schema. Any review or verify eval case built from a real run's gate comparisons (`input.gates`) that includes a failed check will now fail to load with an unrecognized-key error.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone copies `lastGates` from a run with a failing test gate into evals/*/cases.json. loadCases/ReviewCaseFileSchema.parse throws an unrecognized key `failures` error.

findings.title: UI artifact view and land log keep only the last 1,000 tail characters when excerpts exist
findings.detail: The 1,000-character tail was meant for size-limited prompts, but it is also applied where there is no size limit. The ArtifactsPanel shows `failures` plus `output.slice(-1_000)`, and the land log uses `formatGateOutput(r, 9_000)`, which also keeps only 1,000 tail characters and can cut the excerpt itself (room ≈ 7,940 < 8,000), adding a second omission note. Before this change, both showed the full stored 6,000-character tail, so failed tests now show 5,000 fewer tail characters there (counts, the skipped list, the end of stderr). This UI change has no test.
findings.failure_scenario: A failing bun test run whose last 6,000 characters contain useful stderr more than 1,000 characters before the end: the land log and the UI no longer show it.

gold.summary: Unavailable-target diagnostics expose registered credentials in routing API and Setup output.

findings.title: Generic retired-ID filtering also silences previously explicit startup errors (owner-decision removals, model-id-in-prefer)
findings.detail: Unknown IDs in stored operator cells and prefer lists are now dropped with a generic warning. That is the fallback the request asked for, but it also replaces two earlier errors. A stored cell naming a model in `REMOVED_MODELS` (for example `claude/fable`) used to stop startup with that model's owner-decision explanation. Now it is dropped silently, with only the warning 'retired reference: claude/fable is not in the catalog'. A stored prefer containing a model ID (`codex/sol`) used to stop startup with a fix-it hint ('prefer takes provider IDs (use "codex")'). Now it is filtered out silently. The test that covered both messages was deleted rather than adapted.
findings.failure_scenario: A database has `prefer = ["codex/sol"]` from an older release. After upgrading, prefer silently becomes empty instead of showing the hint to use `codex`. Because operatorPrefer is non-null and empty, it also overrides the config's preferProviders.

findings.title: Malformed `[local].remote_host` crashes `limitless local` with a bare 'Invalid URL'
findings.detail: `manageLocal` now runs `new URL(\`http://${host}:8080\`)` to find the matching provider. A host value that isn't a valid URL host (a space, an `ssh://` form, or `host:port`) throws a TypeError before any SSH call. The user sees only 'Invalid URL', which doesn't mention `remote_host`. The old code never parsed the host as a URL.
findings.failure_scenario: I set `[local] remote_host = "bad host"` and ran `limitless local status`. Output: 'Invalid URL'.

findings.title: Remote provider is matched only by an openaiBaseUrl origin on port 8080
findings.detail: `local up` and `local down` find the provider whose `openaiBaseUrl` origin equals `http://<remote_host>:8080`. This breaks in three cases: a LAN provider configured through `ssh_forward` (base URL on 127.0.0.1), one with a different hostname or IP spelling than `remote_host`, or an anthropic-compatible provider (`baseUrl` only). In all three, no provider is matched. Then the health probe goes out without the API key, so llama-server answers 401 and the endpoint shows 'unreachable', and enablement is never updated. `docs/OPERATIONS.md` documents the limitation, but the failure is silent.
findings.failure_scenario: The config defines a `lan` provider with `base_url = "http://192.168.1.5:8080/v1"` and `[local].remote_host = "gpu-box"`. `local up` starts the unit but reports endpoint unreachable (401) and never enables `lan`.

findings.title: Smoke no longer covers any LAN llama.cpp provider
findings.detail: `backendChecks` still loops over a fixed list of provider ids, now `['omlx', 'openrouter']`. Removing the machine-named entry means a config-defined LAN llama.cpp provider, which the docs now present as the supported route, never gets a structured-output smoke check. The removed provider previously got one when healthy.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator configures `lan` as in `docs/GUIDE.md`. `limitless deploy --smoke` never exercises it, so a broken chat template on the LAN server isn't caught.

findings.title: Over the ~120-line source budget, partly from extra scope
findings.detail: About 260 lines of source changed against the requested budget of about 120. Requirement 4 justifies the retired-reference filtering in `retired.ts`, `runtime-policy.ts` and `runtime-catalog.ts`. The new `unavailable` listing in the routing snapshot and the Setup UI rendering go beyond what the request asked for.
findings.failure_scenario: Not a runtime defect; more code to review and maintain.

gold.summary: JSON escaping lets ordinary logged credentials evade literal gate-output redaction.
Line callbacks store pieces of multiline credentials in failure excerpts.

findings.title: Redaction spread to every HTTP/SSE response, state load and prompt input, beyond the single-point design and ~30-line budget
findings.detail: The request asks for gate output to be redacted once, where runGates builds a check result, in about 30 source lines. The change adds about 100 net source lines and also runs redactGateData in other places: on all JSON responses and SSE messages (http.ts serialize), on RunContext state when it loads, on cached stage values, on the whole implement/review/verify prompt inputs and on renderReport. redactGateData is a JSON round trip that strips terminal colour codes from every string. It also adds `confinementError` to any object that has both `ok` and `output` keys, gate result or not. All of this goes well past the request's scope.
findings.failure_scenario: In a quick benchmark, serialising 20,000 events through json() went from 16 ms to 137 ms. Any API object shaped like {ok: true, output: "..."} comes back with an extra confinementError field, and any string with colour codes comes back without them.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint rewrites stored content (diff.patch, pretty JSON)
findings.detail: redactGateArtifact runs on every artifact the endpoint returns, not just gate artifacts. Non-JSON artifacts such as diff.patch go through redactGateOutput, which removes escape sequences and replaces registered-credential strings. JSON artifacts are parsed and written back out compactly. The bytes returned no longer match what was stored.
findings.failure_scenario: A change adds a file with literal ESC bytes (a terminal fixture). GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/diff.patch returns a patch without those bytes, so it no longer applies or matches the reviewed change.

gold.summary: An incomplete terminal escape consumes part of a credential before it can be matched.

findings.title: Output privacy filter now withholds any text containing "[redacted]"
findings.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains the literal "[redacted]". Before, it would redact the string and return it. The request did not ask for this, and no test covers it. MCP status/tools and the digest pass all free text through this filter. So any event message, gate excerpt or report that this change (or the harnesses) already redacted is now hidden completely. The filter is also no longer idempotent: applying it to its own redacted output withholds everything.
findings.failure_scenario: Probe: loadOutputPrivacy()("build failed; see [redacted] token note") returns "[withheld: private text]". Any gate failure that once printed a credential is fully hidden from MCP get_status/digest, not shown with the value masked.

findings.title: Large out-of-scope rewrite: HTTP, SSE, artifacts, run state and reports all pass through redactGateData; budget exceeded about 6x
findings.detail: The request asked to redact once where runGates builds a result, plus the deploy tails, in about 30 net source lines. The source diff adds about 180 net lines. It also sends every HTTP JSON response, every SSE message, every artifact body, the whole RunState (context.ts constructor), checkpoint cache reads, renderReport input and the whole implement/review/verify prompt inputs through a JSON round-trip. That round-trip strips terminal escape sequences from every string, redacts every string, and adds a confinementError field to any object that has `ok` and `output` keys. Most of this goes past the stated out-of-scope line: other output is not gate output. AGENTS.md says to keep to the line b
findings.failure_scenario: Any API consumer now gets responses rewritten by gate-specific logic. Every object with `ok`/`output` gains a `confinementError` key, and escape sequences are removed from unrelated strings such as prompts and patch text in reviewPrompt.

findings.title: Artifact endpoint re-serializes JSON artifacts, losing their formatting
findings.detail: redactGateArtifact parses every artifact as JSON and returns JSON.stringify output with no indentation. Artifacts saved pretty-printed (gates-N.json, baseline-gates.json, review-shadow) are now returned as one long line. The UI's getArtifact displays res.text() directly. Parsing and re-serializing also adds confinementError to gate result objects, and it loses precision on large numbers.
findings.failure_scenario: GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/gates-1.json, stored by JSON.stringify(cmp, null, 2), now returns single-line JSON. That is hard to read in the UI artifact view.

findings.title: confinementError is now always written, reversing the deliberate present-only-when-set format
findings.detail: The old code wrote confinementError only when it was true, with a comment saying this kept results readable by strict schemas and older releases. Now every new GateResult records false or true. This affects cache rows, artifacts, state and events. confinementFailed now treats an explicit false as authoritative and skips the output scan. The current strict eval schema accepts false, so nothing breaks today. Still, the persisted format changed without that being requested, and redactGateData backfills the field into legacy objects.
findings.failure_scenario: An older release, or an external reader that expects the field only when it is true, sees confinementError:false on every stored result after this ships.
